title: Groundhog Bit-Flip Attack: Seeding Infinite Generation Loops in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs through Bit Flips
abstract: arXiv:2608.25276v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures enable scalable and efficient large language models (LLMs) by selectively activating expert sub-networks through a routing mechanism. However, this adaptive design introduces a new attack surface: specific experts become disproportionately correlated with certain tokens (e.g., end-of-sequence), allowing adversaries to manipulate model behavior via lightweight perturbations. In this work, we present \textbf{Groundhog Bit-Flip Attack (GBFA)}, the first bit-flip-based \textit{ Denial-of-Wallet availability attack} against MoE-based LLMs. By identifying and flipping routing-layer bits associated with related expert activations, we demonstrate that GBFA substantially extends the decoding token usage across three different LLM modes: conversational, reasoning, and agentic tasks, while largely preserving semantic fidelity. translated_title: 地鼠位翻转攻击：通过位翻转在混合专家大语言模型中植入无限生成循环
translated_abstract: 混合专家（MoE）架构通过路由机制选择性地激活专家子网络，从而支持可扩展且高效的大语言模型（LLMs）。然而，这种自适应设计引入了新的攻击面：特定专家与某些标记（例如序列结束符）不成比例地关联，使得攻击者能够通过轻量级扰动操纵模型行为。在本工作中，我们提出了**地鼠位翻转攻击（GBFA）**，这是首个针对基于MoE的大语言模型的基于位翻转的*拒绝钱包可用性攻击*。通过识别并翻转与相关专家激活关联的路由层位，我们证明GBFA在三种不同的大语言模型模式（对话、推理和智能体任务）中显著延长了解码标记使用量，同时基本保持语义保真度。在四个主要的真实世界基于MoE的大语言模型中，手动停用平均少于t
tldr: 本文首次提出地鼠位翻转攻击（GBFA），通过翻转MoE模型路由层的少量位，使模型陷入无限生成循环，大幅增加解码计算成本，同时保持输出语义基本不变，构成一种新型的拒绝钱包可用性攻击。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the Groundhog Bit-Flip Attack (GBFA), the first bit-flip-based Denial-of-Wallet availability attack against MoE-based LLMs, which flips a few routing-layer bits to trigger infinite generation loops, significantly increasing decoding cost while preserving semantic fidelity.
